summary: The note describes the joint canonization of Pope John XXIII and Pope John Paul II, held on 27 April 2014. Pope Francis made the decision official on 5 July 2013 after a miracle was attributed to John Paul II's intercession, while John XXIII was canonized for opening the Second Vatican Council. The date was set on 30 September 2013.
one_line: Pope John XXIII and Pope John Paul II were canonized together on 27 April 2014, with Pope Francis making the decision official in 2013.
key_facts: Pope John XXIII lived from 25 November 1881 to 3 June 1963.
Pope John Paul II lived from 18 May 1920 to 2 April 2005.
John XXIII reigned as pope from 1958 to 1963.
John Paul II reigned as pope from 1978 to 2005.
Both popes were also sovereigns of Vatican City during their reigns.
The canonizations of John XXIII and John Paul II were held on 27 April 2014.
Pope Francis made the decision to canonize official on 5 July 2013.
The decision followed recognition of a miracle attributed to the intercession of John Paul II.
John XXIII was canonized for his merits of opening the Second Vatican Council.
The date of the canonization was assigned on 30 September 2013.
